title: Passaic water fight and a loose operation with rigid standards
summary: On closing night at a new Passaic theatre, a water fight with comic Don Rice led to fire hoses and $2,000 in damages; they never played there again.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Were you that kind of rouser, too, yourself?
To a great degree, yeah.
I mean, looking back?
Oh, yeah, yeah.
You were the life of the party?

Well, to some degree. I loved comedy, I enjoyed it very much. And I loved break-ups. That was to me one of the high points of any humor. And I know one time we opened a new theatre in Passaic, New Jersey. It was a brand new
house, it was built near the end of the war. And it was really a miserable week -- wierd people, and it was very difficult.

So the closing night show, we decided to really do one in. And we had a comic on the bill at that point whose name was Don Rice. And he was a comic who worked with a million props. A big arm would come out and grab him. A lot of water props. He'd pick up a phone and say Spitome and he'd get a thing of water in your kisser. Slapstick.
Well, in the closing show, it got into a water fight, which ended up that I had the fire hoses out on that stage. And I think we had to give them about $2,000 for breakage.
Oh, no.
But it was worth it.
(Laughter.)
P.S., we never played the theatre in Passaic again.
How do you spell that?
It's a town in New Jersey, right across the river.
I don't know it.
P-a-s-s-a-i-c.
A lot of this has been carried over to your stage presentation, I know.
Yeah, we're a pretty loose operation. And I think it helps us a great deal particularly in the schools because the kids realize it's not as rigid. The only thing
that's rigid is our determination to play good. That's the a very loose operation. -- but it's I always would hope that an audience would be able to see that we're a non-pressure group.
